clue.text: Stadium music featuring ELO post-break-up, making comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback says the assembled string of letters is read backwards, from end to start
after a break-up the band's letters are split apart and mixed in among the letters of music

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gig at a big arena by the reunited Electric Light Orchestra marks the band's return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring' and 'post-break-up' put E and LO, split apart, into MUSIC to give MUESILOC, which 'making comeback' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coliseum, after Rome's Colosseum, is a name for a large arena or stadium.

clue.text: A soldier in the pampas? That's bananas

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside its letters

parts.note: the pampas are the vast grassy plains of South America
a soldier is a caste of ant, so 'a soldier' is an ant

explanation.surface: Someone spots a single soldier out on the Argentine grasslands and finds it crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like slang for mad, but it is the literal definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantains are a starchy cooking variety of banana.

clue.text: Folk hero regularly seen to split apple with head shot

indicators.note: to split the fruit is to go into the middle of it, breaking it in two
with its head shot off the fruit loses its first letter
regularly means taking every other letter of the word hero

explanation.surface: A William Tell figure splits the apple on someone's head with a single shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' reads as the archer's arrow, but 'with head shot' just removes the fruit's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk and people are synonyms for human beings in general.

clue.text: In our Airbnb we have this climbing wild rose

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters go up the grid, read in reverse
in these words means the letters are found inside the phrase our Airbnb

explanation.surface: A holiday host boasts of a climbing rose growing at their rented-out property.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'ouR AIRBnb' sit RAIRB, which 'climbing' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Briar is the common name for the sweet-briar or dog rose, a wild prickly rose.

clue.text: Rat seen in a river several years running

indicators.note: seen in says one word appears placed inside another

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and also Scotland
a rat is a cad, a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: A rodent has been spotted in a river for several years in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten consecutive years make up a single span of a decade.

clue.text: Edward holds that place is linked with a painter

indicators.note: one word holds another by having it inside

parts.note: Ted is a short form of the name Edward
that place means there, as opposed to here

explanation.surface: Someone called Edward claims a gallery is associated with an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: A painter here is a boat's mooring rope, not an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is the rope at a boat's bow, so a boat tied by one is tied up.

clue.text: This is in every way sacred for audience

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard, a word said aloud sounding like another

parts.note: sacred means holy

explanation.surface: A statement that something is sacred in every respect, as told to listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely, entirely, in every way: all are synonyms.

clue.text: Refuse to break sweat

indicators.note: to break the word up is to shuffle its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone declines to make any effort at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb, decline; it is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse, the noun, is rubbish, the stuff thrown away.

clue.text: Cyclist, say, cycling before and behind

indicators.note: cycling means letters move round from the front of the word to its end

parts.note: a cyclist is an example of a rider
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A cyclist going round and round, with someone ahead and someone at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves RI from the front of RIDER to the back, giving DERRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Derriere, French for rear, is a jokey English word for the backside.

clue.text: Crimes of these receivers?

parts.note: wrongdoings committed by handlers of stolen goods; the clue word Crimes splits as the little word of followed by the slang name for those handlers

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Crimes' as OFFENCES and split it: OF plus a word for receivers of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a dealer in stolen goods is known by this name.

clue.text: Maybe ecology sees Crosophile in landscape catching cold

indicators.note: catching means the word takes another inside it
in means the setter's letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a landscape is a scene
the setter Crosophile refers to themself, which gives I
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: The setter, out in the countryside, sees ecology at work while catching a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into SCENE to give SCIENE, and 'catching' then takes C inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecology is one branch of biology, a natural discipline of study.

clue.text: An ancient royal pub joins a row over hotel

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: over means the word is turned over, its letters running backwards

parts.note: to row is to oar, to propel a boat with oars
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An old king walks into a pub and starts an argument about a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel; it is OAR, the verb, which 'over' turns into RAO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharaohs were the kings of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: I heard a common pet's expensive in Paris for anybody who's striking

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken and gives a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter I, spoken, sounds like the organ of sight
a cat is a common pet
cher is French for expensive

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a cat bought in Paris was costly.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking-looking person or thing draws the gaze of onlookers.

clue.text: Fruit and veg recipe

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable
R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin take, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cookbook instruction for a dish of fruit and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear is a common orchard fruit.

clue.text: 15A refuted

parts.note: the saying at 15 across claims no man is an island; this place in the Irish Sea is literally an island called Man, disproving it

explanation.walkthrough: John Donne's line says no man is an island; the island in the Irish Sea named Man contradicts it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally, an island called Man proves the Donne quotation false.

clue.text: Mainland/North Iona steamship's working and we're all connected

indicators.note: working letters are put to work and rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
North gives its abbreviation N, placed before the island name Iona taken as written
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A ferry runs between the Scottish mainland and the island of Iona, linking everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The words are John Donne's: everyone is part of humanity and none stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Donne's famous line argues that every person is bound up with all others.

clue.text: Regarding request for plain cake?

definitions.meaning: regarding means observing or paying attention to something
someone wanting a plain cake would ask for it not iced, split as not plus icing

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words, NOT ICING.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it and take note, spotting it.

clue.text: Character's new, not initially fully developed

indicators.note: not initially means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: fully developed means mature

explanation.surface: A personality described as fresh and not yet grown up.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's character is their inborn temperament or disposition.

clue.text: A fury flies up with consort high above the ground

indicators.note: in a down clue flying up means the letters go upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: fury means ire, great anger
to consort with someone is to ally with them, and an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A winged Fury from Greek myth soars upward with a companion, far above the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by air, from a height well over the land below.

clue.text: Adolescent initially needs support earlier on

indicators.note: earlier on says the support comes in front of the other piece

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word needs

explanation.surface: A young person mainly needs backing early in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager, aged thirteen to nineteen, is an adolescent.

clue.text: Formerly fortified wine and strong beer

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A drinker once had port and a powerful ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Export was a name for a strong bottled beer, often brewed for sale abroad.

clue.text: Instrument held in one area? Unusual

parts.note: kettling is a police tactic of containing protesters in one spot
rum is British slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a crowd was penned in one place, calling it odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Kettling is the British police tactic of confining a crowd in a small area for hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettledrum, or timpani, is a large orchestral percussion instrument.

clue.text: I'll stay in festival for short time — it's more relaxed

indicators.note: to stay in the word is to take a place within it
for means in place of, one letter standing for another

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A visitor will remain at a festival briefly, finding it calmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Less strained, calmer and more laid-back: a comparative of easy.

clue.text: Bread — a way to get Japanese sort to rise

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of doing something

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters go upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: the yen is the Japanese sort of bread, its currency

explanation.surface: Bread dough as a method of getting a Japanese loaf to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for cash, and 'Japanese sort' means the Japanese sort of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for cash, as is dough.

clue.text: A film for everyone in the round is a wonderful thing

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside its letters

parts.note: a beat is a policeman's regular round
U is the British certificate for a film suitable for all ages

explanation.surface: A family film shown in the round is a marvel.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the UK film rating meaning universal, open to all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaut is Australian slang for something excellent, short for beauty.

clue.text: Tree in WWI battle swathed in gas

indicators.note: swathed in means wrapped inside the letters of another word

parts.note: CS gas is a tear gas
Ypres in Belgium saw several First World War battles

explanation.surface: A lone tree on a First World War battlefield shrouded in poison gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Cypress is a coniferous evergreen, often planted in cemeteries.

clue.text: Give up the burden

definitions.meaning: to give up something is to abstain or hold back from it
the burden of a song is its chorus, the repeated lines

explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' here is the old word for a song's chorus, not a load.
explanation.definitionFit: Desist and abstain match the verb; the noun is a chorus repeated in a song.

clue.text: Brings up return of routine work, ends in more stress

indicators.note: the return of the words means they come back reversed

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine
to run a machine is to work it

indicators.note: ends in means take the last letter of each of the words more and stress

explanation.surface: A tired worker going back to the daily grind ends up more stressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' reads RUTRUN backwards as NURTUR; 'ends in' takes E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to raise, bring up and look after them.

clue.text: A cereal crop, except on pastureland

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
a ley is land sown with grass for a time, used as pasture

explanation.surface: A farmer grows a grain crop everywhere except on grazing fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Barley is a cereal grain grown for animal feed and malting.
